text: Rangers meticulously trained by Fu Yuanshan, tasked with reconnaissance and patrol beyond the Great Bastion. Poisoned arrows and long blades are their weapons of choice against the enemy.

The Wall Rangers are the most agile among the conscripted peasant cavalry, selected for their skill in surviving the Chaos Wastes. They are responsible for reconnaissance and patrol duties in the lands north of the Great Bastion. Almost every one of them shares a background similar to Fu Yuanshan's, harboring a deep hatred of Chaos, and refusing to yield or retreat in the face of the greatest of foes.
As the Dragon Emperor's command reaches Fu Yuanshan, they emerge from the hidden pavilions of Wei Jing to join the army, bringing death to the enemy.

The Oathsworn Riders are the elite among the Grand Dragon Horse cavalry. Once they have accumulated sufficient merit, they receive an invitation from the Dragon Emperor to enter the hidden pavilions and contemplate the primal way of Yin and Yang. But when they emerge, they swear never to reveal a single word of what they learned.
When the Iron Rampart charges upon the battlefield, nothing between heaven and earth can stand in their way.

The Iron Rampart is a heavy cavalry force forged personally by Fu Yuanshan. Compared to the Jade Lancers, it employs techniques from Kun Lan's artisans, equipped with fully cast heavy metal armour. This armour is a marvel that combines multi-layered composite materials with articulated joint designs, a work far ahead of its time. Yet even so, its terrible weight can only be borne by a select few dragon-blooded steeds. Due to its extraordinarily high cost, the Iron Rampart's equipment cannot be used to outfit a standard army on a large scale. On the battlefield, the Iron Rampart can hardly be called cavalry at all - they are engines of destruction driven forward by the power of their warhorses.
They move like thunder, and both city and wilderness tremble at their passing.

The heavy cavalry of Grand Cathay are known as Jade Lancers, their riders drawn from the great cities. Wealthy metropolises such as Fu Zhou and Wei Jing typically station large contingents of Jade Lancers, and even more remote cities in the south and west will raise at least one such unit. Jade Lancers excel not only in open-field battle, but are equally trained to fight in the narrow streets of the cities. Whether in cramped alleys, on bridges, or through the tunnels of city walls, they can launch charges that shatter all resistance. Along the Great Bastion, to withstand the great enemy of Chaos, their armour is forged thicker still than that worn by other Jade Lancers.
This unit possesses the serene attributes of both Yin and Yang.
Heaven's motion is ever vigorous; the noble one ceaselessly strengthens himself.
Earth's condition is receptive devotion; the noble one carries the world with virtue.
Spears rise like a forest, horses roar like dragons - such a formation will tear apart even the most stalwart of enemy lines.
Cavalry who charge howling into the enemy ranks with lances strapped with explosives, the volatile charges violently shattering both armour and morale alike.

Every member of the Fire Lancers is a condemned convict, beyond mercy or pardon. The only thing left for them is to charge into the enemy's ranks wielding lances bound with explosive charges, in hopes of surviving to see another day.
The charge of the Fire Lancers is an attack that burns away both life and future.
In life, they brought endless shame upon Cathay - but in death, they shall bring it glory!
When these heavy riders charge, even death itself cannot get out of the way in time.
This heavy and disciplined formation stands like a looming mountain range. Once it begins to charge, even another mountain in its path would surely be crushed without doubt!

What drives this mountain-like formation forward is a madness born of the most rigorous discipline. To master the extraordinary ferocity of their exotic mounts, these peerless warriors, once clad in heavy iron and mounted, will only dismount in death. In exchange, they gain, in mortal flesh, a strength equal to or even surpassing the filth of Chaos. They often bring victory to Cathay, yet also reveal just how heavy and bitter the price of that victory can be.
The very existence of these dark riders heralds death itself. Heavy, unyielding, slow, and unstoppable.
